# The citation toolchain, pinned — and pinned in both halves deliberately.
#
# specs/specs_generated.yaml is a generated file that lives in the tree, and
# `apycite extract --frozen` compares it byte for byte. Those bytes are a
# function of the reader's version: apysource decides each source's URL and
# media type, apycite decides the ordering and the labels. An unpinned reader
# therefore makes every upstream release a silent, unreviewed change to a
# committed file — the diff lands on whichever pull request happens to run
# first, blamed on an author who touched nothing near it.
#
# Pinning apycite alone does not close this. apycite floors apysource with no
# ceiling, so `pip install apycite` pulls a new apysource the moment one is
# published, even when apycite itself has not moved. Both lines are load-bearing.
#
# This is not a migration shim. When the toolchain moves forward, the pin moves
# forward in a commit of its own, alongside the regenerated file it produces —
# which is exactly the review the unpinned form skipped. APYCITE.md's A10 is the
# precedent: 0.8.0 fixed one extraction defect and shipped another in the same
# tag, so for one release the tool lost section labels it had just gained.
#
# 0.10.0/0.6.0 regenerates nothing, and that is worth stating because the
# paragraph above leads you to expect otherwise: this pair adds a check rather
# than changing what extraction writes down, so specs_generated.yaml is
# byte-identical and `extract --frozen` passes across the bump. What it adds is
# the nightly job's `Document supersession` row — whether each cited document is
# still the one in force. Six of ours are not; see .github/workflows/citations.yml
# for why that is a warning and not a failure.

apycite==0.6.0
apysource==0.10.0
